sentences.text: 1  JUDGMENT
Though matter is listed for arguments, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the petitioner seeking to modify the impugned judgment and award dated 31.08.2015 passed by the MACT-VI, Vijaypur, in MVC No.413/2006.
3.
The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the tribunal.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that impugned judgment and award is contrary to the law and material evidence placed before the Court.
Same is vitiated insofar as in not awarding compensation in claim petition.
Learned MACT has not justified in dismissing the claim petition on the ground that there is no proper explanation in delay in lodging the complaint.

The said finding is contrary to the records after remanding the matter, the appellant has lead a fresh evidence before MACT and he has clearly stated in para No.4 of his evidence that respondent No.1 had assured that he will pay the entire medical expenses and did not lodge the complaint before the police authority and finally, he has refused after discharge of the appellant from the hospital he has refused to make payment of the medical expenses.
Learned MACT has not appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and dismissed the claim petition.
Further it is submitted that delay in lodging the complaint should not be treated as fatal to file the claim petition.

To substantiate his arguments he relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAVI v. BADRINARAAN AND OTHERS reported in (2011 Kant. M.A.C. 379 (SC) and sought for allowing this appeal.
5.

6. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the appellant has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award?
(2) Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for in the claim petition?
(3) What order/award?

8.
I have carefully gone through the materials placed before this Court.

Present appellant Azamat @
Hazmat, S/o. Basheerahamad Khadeem had filed a claim petition in MVC No.413/2006 before the MACT IV, Vijayapur.
The tribunal has passed the judgment and award in MVC No.413/2006 and awarded compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed in MVC No.413/2006, the insurance company has preferred an appeal before this Court in MFA No.30565/2009 (MV).

This court has passed an order on 03.04.2013 holding that judgment and award question requires to set aside and to remand case back to the tribunal to frame issues based on insurance company's specific contention and decide the issue on merit and dispose of the same in accordance with law.

After remanding this case,
the tribunal has framed the additional issues and claimant has also adduced the evidence.
In all 2 witnesses are examined as PW1 and PW2 and 8 documents got marked as Exs.P-1 to P-8.

On closure of claimant's side evidence, respondents have not adduced evidence on their behalf but the insurance policy is marked as Ex.R-1.
10.

A perusal of the materials placed before the Tribunal which is crystal clear that on the basis of the private complaint lodged by the appellant Azamat @ Hazmat, S/o. Basheerahamad filed under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. before the JMFC, Bijapur.
The case was referred to concerned police for investigation.

On receipt of this complaint filed by the appellant, Bijapur police have registered the case in Crime No.26/2006 against the driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-28/A-1623 for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and 134 of Motor Vehicles Act.
11. The alleged accident took place on 26.12.2005.

Immediately the injured has admitted to the hospital with the history of motor vehicle accident and he has admitted to the hospital on 26.12.2005 at 8.30 p.m. in the Basanagouda Patil Memorial Hospital and he has taken treatment in the hospital after discharge from the hospital on 10.01.2006.
This injury certificate is marked as Ex.P-5.

When the injured has admitted with the history of motor vehicle accident, it is the duty of the concerned medical officer to intimate the same to the police, but the concerned medical officer has failed to discharge his duty.
For that tribunal ought not to have rejected the claim petition.

12. In Ex.P-2 the complaint filed by this appellant he has clearly explained as to the delay in filing this complaint stating that the respondent No.1 has assured that he will pay the entire medical expenses.
Hence, did not lodge the complaint before the police authorities.
Finally when he refused to pay the same, he lodged a complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate in accordance with law.
13. On thorough investigation the IO has submitted the charge sheet against the accused for the commission of alleged offences punishable u/s 279, 338 IPC and Sec. 134 of MV Act.
RW1 - owner of the vehicle has admitted that he is the owner of the of the auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-28/A-1623 and denied the rash and negligent act on the part of the accident.

14. Tribunal has observed in the impugned judgment that even after remand of the case the pleadings are not got amended to the effect that private complaint was filed and that there was a delay in filing such complaint.
Further it has observed that if reasons are not mentioned in the claim petition, adducing evidence without pleadings is not accepted.
But this observation made by the tribunal cannot be accepted.
In motor vehicle accident cases the strict pleading is not required.
The claimants have furnished all the particulars as shown in Rule 232- C(1) Form 63-C of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles rules, 1989.
Apart from this, appellant has pleaded in para 22 of the claim petition as to the details of this accident.

With regard to the delay in filing the FIR is concerned, I have gone through the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RAVI v. BADRINARAAN AND OTHERS reported in (2011 Kant. M.A.C. 379 (SC) wherein at para 21 of the judgment the Apex Court has observed as under:
"21.

entities.text: RAVI v. BADRINARAAN AND OTHERS reported in (2011 Kant. M.A.C. 379 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgement of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more.

significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
- 10 - 15.

Considering the evidence placed b the appellants before the Tribunal and keeping in mind the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court, I am of the considered view that appellant has proved that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA- 28/A-1623 by which the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: The doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury Nos.2 and 3 are simple in nature.

Ex.P-7 is the disability certificate issued by PW2- Dr.A.A.Magi, Ortho Surgeon, Bijapur, in which it is observed as under:
"In my opinion injury no(1) is grievous in nature, injury no.2 and 3 are simple in nature, the are 0-6 hours old in age and might have been caused by having met with hand and right surface & high velocity."
18.
Considering the nature of injuries and disability certificate by PW5, it is just and proper to determine the disability at 10% to the whole body.
19. Considering the age and occupation of the appellant, it is just and proper to assess the income of the injured at Rs.3,000/- per month and the multiplier application is '18'.
The same would result in Rs.64,800/- (Rs.3,000/- x 12 x 18 x 10%), which is rounded off to Rs.65,000/-.

Accordingly,
appellant is entitled to compensation of Rs.65,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability.

Considering the nature of injuries, pain and suffering, medical expenses, period of taking treatment, it is just and proper to award the compensation as under:

Thus, appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,64,000/-.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in partly affirmative.
22. The tribunal has framed the issue regarding violation of policy conditions as additional issue No.2.

The tribunal has held that respondent No.2 - insurance company has failed to prove that there is a violation of policy conditions as against this and also the tribunal has answered additional issue No.2 in the negative.

RE. POINT NO.3:
23.

For the aforestated reasons and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(1) The appeal is allowed in part.
(2) The judgment and award dated 31.08.2015 passed by MACT-VI, Vijaypur, in MVC No.413/2006, is set aside.

(3) The appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,64,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation. (4) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
(5) Respondent No.2 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment before the tribunal.
- 14 - (6) Since the claim petition is filed in the year 2006, the tribunal is directed to release the deposited amount, if any, by the insurance company in MFA No.30565/2009.
(7) Registry to send back the TCR along with the copy of the judgment.
(8) Registry to draw the decree accordingly.
